title: WPMS/1603/2009 of PREM LAL Vs OM PRAKASH

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1603 of 2009
Prem Lal ...Petitioner

Versus
Om Prakash ......Respondent
Present: Mr. M.C. Pande, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. B.P.S.
Mer, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for the respondent.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
 In this writ petition the petitioner who is the
defendant in the suit for cancellation of sale deed,
prays for quashing of the order dated 19.08.2008,
passed by the learned Trial Court in O.S. No. 209 of
2006 "Om Prakash Vs. Prem Lal" and the Order dated
09.07.2009 passed by the Additional District Judge/
F.T.C in Civil Revision No. 55 of 2008 "Prem Nath Vs.
Om Prakash" by virtue of which the learned Court
below the suit in question while framing the issues, had
framed the issue No. 1 to the following effect:-
"As to whether the suit has been insufficiently
valued and the Court fees paid therein is
insufficient".
2. Learned Court below, while deciding the
issue No. 1 as preliminary issue by the order dated
19.08.2008 has held that since the land which was
conveyed by a sale deed was an agricultural land and

2
thus in view of Section 7(iv-A) of the Suit Valuation Act,
the Court fees paid was sufficient.
3. Accordingly the issue was decided against
the defendant/petitioner, which was put to challenge by
the petitioner in the revision being Revision No. 55 of
2008, which too has recorded a finding almost identical
to the finding recorded by the learned Trial Court.
4. The petitioner preferred a writ petition on
06.09.2009 and the same was opposed by the
plaintiff/caveator through his counsel for the
respondent which was filed on 06.08.2009. After
hearing him he sought an adjournment on 17.09.2009
and then yet again on 05.10.2009 sought adjournment.
Now almost 8 years have lapsed, no counter has been
filed denying the pleadings raised, in the writ petition.
Hence, this Court has got no option except to agree
with the grounds pleaded by the learned counsel for
the petitioner in the writ petition.
5. It is settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the
judgment reported in AIR 1993(2) SC 2592 in "Smt.
Naseem Bano Vs. State of U.P. and Others" held
that when a party appears to a litigation and does not
controvert the pleadings raised in the writ, it will

3
amount to be an admission of the pleadings. However
the factual backdrop which has been argued by the
learned counsel for the petitioner is that the sale deed
dated 12.04.2006 by virtue of which the property
measuring 1.113 hectares situated in village Rampura,
Tehsil Kichha, District Udham Singh Nagar has been
conveyed, was not depicting the actual consideration of
the property.
6. Learned Senior counsel for the petitioner
further submitted that let us presume that the
consideration of sale deed was correct which has been
given in the sale deed then at least if a suit for its
cancellation is preferred then the valuation of the suit
has to be based on ad valorem and not on the basis of
the revenue which the land will be fetching was for the
reason that the scrutiny before the Court below is for
cancellation of sale deed in the suit and it is with
regards to a registered documents which is sought to
be set aside / cancelled by the Court. So subject matter
of judicial scrutiny in the registered document sought to
be cancelled hence valuation of suit has to be on the
basis of valuation given in the sale deed itself.
7. In that view of the matter this Court feels that
the suit since being a suit for cancellation of sale deed

4
ought to have been valued on the basis of valuation of
the documents and not on the basis of the valuation of
the property and its nature as recorded in revenue
records.
8. Thus the impugned orders dated 19.08.2008
in C.S. No. 209 of 2006 - Om Prakash Vs. Prem Lal,
passed by learned trial Court and order dated
09.07.2009 passed by the Additional District
Judge/First F.T.C in Civil Revision No. 55 of 2008 -
Prem Lal Vs. Om Prakash are quashed. The writ
petition is allowed. Learned trial Court is directed to
levy an appropriate Court fee, based on the documents
sought to be cancelled and the District Judge is
directed to place the matter before the Court of
competent jurisdiction for its expeditious adjudication.
9. No order as to costs.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
07.10.2017
Mahinder/
